transcript:
[doctor] Hi there, I see you're here today for dizziness and giddiness. Can you tell me more about what's been going on?

[patient] Hi, yes. I've been feeling really dizzy and giddy for the past five days. It gets pretty severe, especially in the afternoons, and it's enough to keep me from working and doing daily tasks.

[doctor] Hmm, that sounds tough. How long do these episodes usually last?

[patient] They last several hours each time.

[doctor] I see. Are there any other symptoms that come with the dizziness?

[patient] Yes, sometimes I see double and have a hard time concentrating. I also get headaches.

[doctor] Alright. How often do these episodes happen in a day?

[patient] Multiple times, maybe three or four times a day.

[doctor] Okay. I'm going to ask you a few more questions to get a clearer picture. Have you noticed any changes in your vision besides the double vision?

[patient] No, just the double vision.

[doctor] Any issues with your hearing or ringing in your ears?

[patient] No, none at all.

[doctor] How about nausea or vomiting?

[patient] No, I haven't had any nausea or vomiting.

[doctor] Got it. Let's talk a bit about your general health. Have you had any fever, chills, or signs of infection?

[patient] No, I haven't had any of those.

[doctor] Alright. Now, have you been feeling especially tired or fatigued?

[patient] Yes, I've been feeling really tired, but I think that's because of the dizziness.

[doctor] That makes sense. Do you have any medical conditions that we should be aware of?

[patient] No, I don't have any major medical conditions.

[doctor] Are you currently taking any medications?

[patient] No, I don't take any medications regularly.

[doctor] Okay. Do you have a family history of any medical conditions like heart disease or stroke?

[patient] Yes, my father has high blood pressure and my mother had a stroke a few years ago.

[doctor] Thanks for sharing that. I'm going to take a look at your vital signs and perform a physical examination now. 

[patient] Sure, go ahead.

[doctor] Alright, your blood pressure is elevated at 150/95 mmHg, and your heart rate is also elevated. Let me check your neurological functions. Okay, I see a slight nystagmus and some mild unsteadiness when you're walking.

[patient] What does that mean?

[doctor] Nystagmus is a condition where there is involuntary movement of the eyes, and it can be associated with dizziness. The mild unsteadiness could be related to your dizziness as well. 

[patient] Oh, I see.

[doctor] Your ENT exam shows no signs of infection or inflammation, so that's good news. 

[patient] That's a relief.

[doctor] Based on your symptoms and the findings from the examination, it seems like you might be experiencing a hypertensive crisis, which means your high blood pressure could be causing your dizziness and other symptoms.

[patient] Oh, wow. What should I do?

[doctor] First, we need to adjust your medication to better control your blood pressure. I'm going to prescribe Lisinopril 20 mg to be taken once a day, and also add Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg once a day.

[patient] Alright, I can do that.

[doctor] I also want to run some additional tests to rule out other possible causes. We'll order a comprehensive metabolic panel and a lipid panel to check for any metabolic issues.

[patient] Okay, what else?

[doctor] I'd also like to get a CT scan of your brain to make sure there's no central nervous system cause for your symptoms, like a hemorrhage or stroke.

[patient] That sounds serious.

[doctor] It's just a precaution, but it's important to rule out these possibilities. 

[patient] I understand.

[doctor] I also recommend that you follow up with us in one week to reassess your blood pressure and symptoms. 

[patient] Alright, I'll do that.

[doctor] Additionally, I'd like to refer you to a cardiologist, Dr. Anthony Martinez, for further evaluation and management of your hypertension.

[patient] Okay, I'll see Dr. Martinez.

[doctor] In the meantime, make sure to take your medications as prescribed. Avoid smoking and limit your alcohol consumption. Try to reduce processed and fried foods in your diet and work on improving your sleep hygiene.

[patient] Got it. 

[doctor] And if your symptoms worsen or if you develop any new symptoms, call the clinic immediately.

[patient] Will do. Thank you, doctor.

[doctor] You're welcome. Take care, and we'll see you in a week for your follow-up.

[patient] Thanks, I'll see you then.

[doctor] Alright, take care. Goodbye.

[patient] Goodbye.
